content.title: Lecture 2 Homework Review
content.content:
Lecture 2 Homework Review
Sort out what changed and what did not in LoRA training, and connect it to today's exercise (first ~5 min).
Basic
Change one of lora_r, lr, or num_train_epochs in CONFIG, retrain, and compare the two rates, final loss, and training time with the original
Implementation
Replace the FAQ and questions with your own topic (about 5 items), train, and compare before and after. Also describe how you made the "no basis" questions
Advanced
Build Q&A data from the course glossary, train on it, prepare your own evaluation questions, and compare before and after. Also compare with a search-based approach
Do now: while listening, click Sync fork on your fork and start Codespaces (takes a few minutes; preparation for Step 1)
Focus on "what changed" and "why". This is not about guessing the correct numbers

On your fork on GitHub: Sync fork → Update branch
If Sync fork shows “Discard commits”, do not click it.
Clicking it deletes your commits. Start using the method in Step 1 under “If main is broken or the previous lecture is unfinished”.

content.title: Exercise review: results from the instructor's T4 run
content.content:
Exercise review: results from the instructor's T4 run
Compared on the same 21 questions with the same generation settings. Only the adapter (on/off) differed.
0.095 → 1.0
Format compliance rate (format_rate)
0 → 0.905
Content accuracy rate (content_rate)  19 / 21 questions
None

content.title: Exercise review: classify the remaining failures and organize the causes
content.content:
Exercise review: classify the remaining failures and organize the causes
Classify the failures remaining after training into 3 types and sort out why they remained.
Asserting without basis
Applies a sentence from another item to a question not in the FAQ
Declares needs_review: false
Evading despite a basis
Says "not stated" for a question that is in the FAQ
Sets needs_review: true
Broken format
Missing keys, extra sentences added
needs_review becomes the string "false"
The 2 questions remaining in the instructor's run (both assertions)
"When are grades released?" → asserts from the deadline FAQ / "Do office hours require a reservation?" → asserts from the office hours FAQ
The training data is 14 items (4 without basis). The format is learned, but telling whether a basis exists is harder to learn

content.title: Basic walkthrough: change one setting and compare
content.content:
Basic walkthrough: change one setting and compare
A falling loss is not the same as rising evaluation accuracy. Compare under the same conditions.
Setting to change
Meaning
What to look at
lora_r
Rank of the adapter matrices (expressiveness)
trainable% and training time. A higher r does not always raise accuracy
lr
Size of the weight update per step
Too large makes loss unstable. Too small and the format is not learned
num_train_epochs
How many passes over the training data
Even if loss keeps falling, accuracy may plateau or drop (overfitting)
How to compare: change only one. Line up the two rates, final loss, and training time, and check the conditions in result.json's config
Before retraining: Runtime → Restart session and run from the top (the trained adapter is still loaded)

content.title: Implementation walkthrough: how to make "no basis" questions
content.content:
Implementation walkthrough: how to make "no basis" questions
Using only questions unrelated to the FAQ cannot test whether the model asks for confirmation or makes an assertion.
Too-easy example
A topic unrelated to the FAQ
Example: "What do you recommend at the cafeteria?"
Any model easily answers "not stated"
Example that tests judgment
A topic near the FAQ, but not written in it
Example: "When are grades released?" (a deadline FAQ exists)
How to split the data
Do not use the same sentences for training and evaluation
Split paraphrases into train / valid / test by template
The 2 questions remaining in the instructor's run: both asked about something near the FAQ but not written in it
Mixing in near-topic questions that are not written lets you test whether the model asserts

content.title: Advanced walkthrough: train it or let it search?
content.content:
Advanced walkthrough: train it or let it search?
Training on the glossary and searching it each have strengths and weaknesses.
Aspect
Train (Lecture 2)
Search (Lecture 3)
Adding / fixing terms
Retrain
Just fix the data
Wording differences
Depends on training data paraphrases
Depends on how you search
Showing the basis
Difficult
Can show search results
Answer format and tone
Easy to instill
Instruct via prompt
Often combined. Today we make "search" a tool for the agent

content.title: Agent = model + loop + tools
content.content:
Agent = model + loop + tools
The LLM chooses a tool and requests the call; the program runs it. The LLM sees the result and decides what is next.
Lecture 1: app.ask
Ask
→
LLM
→
Answer
One LLM call
Lecture 3: app.agent
Ask
→
LLM
→
Run the tool (program)
→
LLM
→
Answer
Repeat “LLM → tool → LLM” until the needed information is gathered (agent loop)
1
Decides whether to call a tool from its name, description (docstring), and argument types
Model
2
The program runs the tool and returns the result to the model
Tool
3
Multiple LLM calls per question
Loop
Tools in app/agent.py
search_glossary: search the glossary
get_lecture_summary: key points of a session
make_quiz: added today
Multiple LLM calls per question. Hits the rate limit sooner than in Lecture 1

content.title: Step 2: Ask the agent the same question as in Lecture 1
content.content:
Step 2: Ask the agent the same question as in Lecture 1
Ask the agent, which can search the glossary, the same question as Lecture 1’s app.ask, and compare the answers.
Command
uv run python -m app.agent "What are the “3 levels” in the AIE2026 course homework?"
Lecture 1: app.ask (plain LLM)
Does not know the course
Says “I don’t know” or gives a plausible general answer
Lecture 3: app.agent
Searches the glossary, then answers

content.title: Step 3: Read the tool calls with --trace
content.content:
Step 3: Read the tool calls with --trace
Read which tool was called with which arguments, and how many times the LLM was called for one question.
Command
uv run python -m app.agent --trace "What is the difference between LoRA and QLoRA?"
Example output (calls and counts vary per run)
(answer text)
--- trace ---
[tool call]   search_glossary({'query': 'LoRA'})
[tool call]   search_glossary({'query': 'QLoRA'})
[tool return] search_glossary -> [{"term": "LoRA", …
[usage] RunUsage(… requests=2, tool_calls=2)
[tool call]
The model requested “this tool, with these arguments”
[tool return]
The program ran the tool and returned the result to the model
requests
Number of LLM calls for one question
Why two separate searches: the instructions say to always search before answering and to look up one term at a time. See the next slide
More requests means more response time, cost, and rate-limit pressure

content.title: Step 3 supplement: INSTRUCTIONS and docstrings that shape behavior
content.content:
Step 3 supplement: INSTRUCTIONS and docstrings that shape behavior
The model’s guidance lives in two places. The behavior you saw with --trace is set by the sentences written there.
app/agent.py (around line 31): instructions for the whole agent
INSTRUCTIONS = """\
You are a learning support agent for the AI Engineering Pilot Course (AIE2026).
- Always check the glossary with search_glossary before answering about terms or course-specific information.
- Use get_lecture_summary when asked about the content of a session.
- If something is absent from the glossary, say "It is not in the glossary" instead of making assertions based on guesses.
- End your answer by indicating the relevant session (Lecture NN).
- Guide learners with hints on how to think, rather than writing homework answers for them.
"""
app/tools.py: tool description (docstring)
def search_glossary(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the course glossary and return definitions and the sessions that cover the terms.

    Use before answering about AI engineering terms or words specific to this course (AIE2026).
    Put only one term to look up in query (for example, "LoRA").
    """
“Always check the glossary with search_glossary”
→ In Steps 2 and 3, search_glossary was called before answering.
“End your answer by indicating the relevant session (Lecture NN)”
→ In Step 2, the answer ended with the relevant lecture number.
docstring: “Put only one term to look up in query”
→ In Step 3, LoRA and QLoRA were searched separately.
In the homework (Basic), rewrite this text and compare --trace for the same question.

content.title: Step 4: Write and register the make_quiz tool
content.content:
Step 4: Write and register the make_quiz tool
Let the agent build a question from the glossary when asked for a review question.
1
Add the function make_quiz(lecture: int) -> str to app/tools.py
2
Write “when and why to use it” in the docstring (the model reads it)
3
From the glossary (load_glossary()), collect the terms of the given lecture and pick one
4
Return a question like “What does X mean?” and the answer (that term’s definition)
5
Register it at the TODO in app/agent.py (agent.tool_plain)
Example return value of make_quiz(2)
{"question": "What does “PEFT” mean?",
"answer": "Not all of the model's parameters, …"}
Starter code (the docstring becomes the description)
def make_quiz(lecture: int) -> str:
    """Pick one term from the given lecture and
    return a review question and its answer.

    Use when asked for review questions, such as
    “Give me a review question for Lecture 2”.
    """
    # 1. Collect terms from load_glossary() matching lecture
    # 2. Pick one (random.choice)
    # 3. Return Q and answer as a string (e.g. json.dumps)
You may use Copilot. Read and understand suggested code before accepting it

content.title: Step 5: Check that make_quiz gets called
content.content:
Step 5: Check that make_quiz gets called
Check first that the model can see it, then that it is actually called, and finally that the tests pass.
1
uv run python -m app.agent --list-tools
make_quiz and its docstring are displayed
2
uv run python -m app.agent --trace "Give me one review question from Lecture 02"
[tool call] make_quiz({'lecture': 2})
3
uv run pytest -q
All passed (the added tool does not fail either)
What the pytest in 3 checks: without using an API key, it calls every tool, including the new make_quiz, with dummy arguments (such as lecture=0) and checks that none fail with an error. If it fails on a nonexistent lecture, add handling for when there are no terms
If make_quiz is not called
Not in the list from 1 → not registered in app/agent.py
In the list but not called → describe concretely when to use it in the docstring. Add “Use make_quiz when asked for a review question” to INSTRUCTIONS

content.title: Troubleshooting
content.content:
Troubleshooting
An agent calls the LLM several times per question, so it hits the rate limit sooner than in Lecture 1.
Symptom
Fix
Rate limit reached (429)
Wait about 1 minute and rerun
Model is overloaded (503)
Wait a bit and rerun. If it persists, run with AIE_MODEL=gemini-3.1-flash-lite
Environment variable GEMINI_API_KEY not found
Check that the secret’s Repository access includes your fork → stop Codespaces and reopen
make_quiz is not called
Check it is listed with --list-tools. If not, you forgot to register it; if it is, review the docstring and INSTRUCTIONS
lec03-start not found
Check that you ran git fetch … tag lec03-start from Step 1
a branch named 'lec03' already exists
lec03 already exists. Switch to it with git switch lec03
git pull shows CONFLICT
Undo with git merge --abort (your changes are kept) → start with the method on the right of Step 1 (lec03-start)
pytest fails
Read the last line of the error. Common causes: a missing import, a mistyped function name

content.title: Homework: complete any one
content.content:
Homework: complete any one
Pick one of three levels (Basic / Implementation / Advanced). Completing any one finishes the homework.
Level
Content
Basic
Rewrite INSTRUCTIONS in app/agent.py or the tool docstrings in app/tools.py from the exercise. Run the same question with --trace, then compare and record how tool calls and answers change
Implementation
Build a save_learning_log tool that saves learning records to the learning_log/ folder. Saving is hard to undo, so ask the user to confirm first (Pydantic AI’s requires_approval=True)
Advanced
Do one of the following. (a) Use the same instructions and tools as the exercise agent, rewrite only the agent-building part with Google’s ADK, run it with adk run, and compare the code and answers. (b) Run the coding agent Pi in Codespaces and compare Pi’s published system prompt with your agent’s INSTRUCTIONS
How to proceed: explained on the next 3 slides. Write your submission in the “Homework” section of lectures/03/answer.md

content.title: Homework steps (Basic / Implementation)
content.content:
Homework steps (Basic / Implementation)
Record what you changed and the result, checking against the --trace output.
Basic: change INSTRUCTIONS or a docstring and compare
Change only one place at a time, run the same question with --trace, and compare
Places to change: INSTRUCTIONS in app/agent.py (around line 31) and the tool docstrings in app/tools.py
Example: delete the “Always check the glossary with search_glossary” line from INSTRUCTIONS. Does it answer without searching?
Example: change “Put only one term” in the docstring to “Put several terms.” How does the number of searches change?
Record how tools are called (order, count, arguments) and how the answer changes
Implementation: ask for confirmation before saving
Create save_learning_log in app/tools.py and register it in app/agent.py with requires_approval=True
When this tool is called, execution pauses for approval and DeferredToolRequests is returned
So add DeferredToolRequests to the agent’s output_type (code below)
In the CLI, ask the user whether to save, then pass the result back and continue
Writing output_type
from pydantic_ai import Agent, DeferredToolRequests
agent = Agent(instructions=INSTRUCTIONS,
              output_type=[str, DeferredToolRequests])
Reference: Pydantic AI official docs, “Deferred Tools”, Human-in-the-Loop Tool Approval (pydantic.dev/docs/ai/tools-toolsets/deferred-tools/)

content.title: Homework steps (Advanced a): rebuild with ADK
content.content:
Homework steps (Advanced a): rebuild with ADK
Use the same instructions and tools as the exercise agent and rewrite only the agent-building part with ADK.
Scope
Content
Reuse as is
INSTRUCTIONS in app/agent.py, and search_glossary and get_lecture_summary in app/tools.py (also make_quiz if you built it in the exercise)
Write new
In the adk_agent/glossary_agent/ folder, create agent.py (code on the right) and __init__.py (one line: from . import agent)
Not needed
Command features such as --trace, tests, and tools with approval. Don’t change files in app/
Compare
The code (how instructions and tools are passed) and how the answers differ from the same questions in the exercise
adk_agent/glossary_agent/agent.py
from google.adk.agents import Agent
from app import tools
from app.agent import INSTRUCTIONS
root_agent = Agent(
    model="gemini-3.5-flash-lite",
    name="glossary_agent",
    instruction=INSTRUCTIONS,
    tools=[...],  # tools used in the exercise
)
Run (from the repo root)
PYTHONPATH=. uv run --with google-adk \
  adk run adk_agent/glossary_agent
Type a question and press Enter. Type exit to quit. The first run takes about 1 minute to fetch ADK
ADK changed significantly in 2.0. Web articles may contain outdated information that doesn’t reflect the changes, so implementing from the official docs (adk.dev) should reduce mistakes

content.title: Homework steps (Advanced b): run Pi in Codespaces
content.content:
Homework steps (Advanced b): run Pi in Codespaces
Pi edits files and runs commands without asking for confirmation. Try it inside Codespaces.
1
Install
npm install -g --ignore-scripts \
  @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent
2
Launch
pi
3
Set the model
In Pi, type /model and choose a Gemini model. The Codespaces secret GEMINI_API_KEY is used as the API key as is
4
Compare
Compare Pi’s system prompt (packages/coding-agent/src/core/system-prompt.ts in github.com/earendil-works/pi) with your INSTRUCTIONS, and record what is written and what is not
Pi official docs: github.com/earendil-works/pi/tree/main/packages/coding-agent/docs
